files.why: Once the invoice loads, call fetchUpcomingAppointments(invoice.clientId, new Date()) from the @slices/scheduling public alias and expose the soonest AppointmentSummary — the canonical cross-slice read exactly mirroring useInvoiceList.ts.
Render a small next-appointment panel from the composable's summary (Card + formatDate already imported), including empty/loading handling.

uncertain: Whether to keep the panel inline in InvoiceDetailView.vue or extract a component. Per README worked example #2 and rule 6, inline-from-summary is correct first; a reusable 'next appointment' component about scheduling display would belong in scheduling/ui and be exposed via scheduling/index.ts, never created under billing. I chose inline because the request is one panel on one page.

scheduling/index.ts is intentionally NOT in my list: I verified it already exports both fetchUpcomingAppointments(clientId, now) and the AppointmentSummary type (which already carries start/resourceId/durationMinutes/status). It would only need touching if product wants a display field that AppointmentSummary lacks.
questions: What exactly is 'next' — just the single soonest scheduled appointment, or a short upcoming list? And which fields to show (start date/time, resource, duration, status)?

What should render when the client has no upcoming appointment, or when the scheduling fetch fails/loads slowly — hide the panel, show an empty state, or a skeleton independent of the invoice's own loading state?

The repo currently has tests only for core/ and mappers/ (no UI or composable tests). Should this add a useInvoiceDetail composable test for the new join, or is leaving UI untested consistent with team convention?
